claim_judgments.rationale: An employer operating in a general industry workplace where no OSHA standard in Part 1910 specifically mandates an emergency action plan would be required to maintain one under the draft's unconditional rule, whereas the source requires one only 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one'. The draft drops this critical condition of applicability and also omits the sentence establishing that § 1910.38's requirements apply to each such plan. Consequently, scope and summary are erroneous.

An employer with 10 or fewer employees who chooses to communicate the emergency action plan orally would violate the draft's unqualified requirement that the plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available for review, whereas the source explicitly exempts such employers by allowing oral communication. The draft correctly incorporates the governing applicability lead-in from § 1910.38(a) but fails to qualify the written mandate with the explicit small-employer exception, making the summary incomplete.

No supported contrast found. The draft correctly reflects that an employer with 10 or fewer employees is permitted to communicate the emergency action plan orally to employees when an OSHA standard requires an emergency action plan under 29 CFR Part 1910. Modality, actor, numerical threshold of 10 or fewer employees, and action are all accurately preserved.

No supported contrast found. The draft accurately represents the employer's duty under § 1910.38(e) to designate and train employees to assist in a safe and orderly evacuation of other employees, governed by the general applicability condition in § 1910.38(a). All dimensions match the source text.

unit_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 omits the essential conditional prerequisite 'whenever an OSHA standard in this part requires one' and omits the provision applying the section's requirements to each such plan.
Claim C0001 covers the core written format and workplace availability requirements but omits the explicit statutory exception permitting oral communication for employers with 10 or fewer employees.
Claim C0002 fully and faithfully retains the permission for employers with 10 or fewer employees to communicate the plan orally.
No draft claim addresses the minimum requirement in § 1910.38(c)(1) to include procedures for reporting a fire or other emergency.
No draft claim addresses the minimum requirement in § 1910.38(c)(2) to include procedures for emergency evacuation, including type of evacuation and exit route assignments.
No draft claim addresses the minimum requirement in § 1910.38(c)(3) to include procedures for employees who remain to operate critical plant operations before evacuating.
No draft claim addresses the minimum requirement in § 1910.38(c)(4) to include procedures to account for all employees after evacuation.
No draft claim addresses the minimum requirement in § 1910.38(c)(5) to include procedures to be followed by employees performing rescue or medical duties.
No draft claim addresses the minimum requirement in § 1910.38(c)(6) regarding employee contact names or job titles for plan information and duty explanations.
No draft claim addresses the employer duty in § 1910.38(d) to have and maintain an employee alarm system.
No draft claim addresses the employee alarm system requirements in § 1910.38(d) to use distinctive signals and comply with § 1910.165.
Claim C0003 fully and accurately captures the requirement in § 1910.38(e) to designate and train employees to assist in safe and orderly evacuation under the applicable scope.
No draft claim addresses the requirement in § 1910.38(f)(1) to review the plan when developed or when an employee is initially assigned to a job.
No draft claim addresses the requirement in § 1910.38(f)(2) to review the plan when an employee's responsibilities under the plan change.
No draft claim addresses the requirement in § 1910.38(f)(3) to review the plan when the plan is changed.
